lines.japanese: 小鳩は今日が終業式だったので、柳木原の改札前で待ち合わせした。
lines.english: Kobato’s school term ended today, so we’d arranged to meet by the ticket gates at Yanagihara.

lines.japanese: 彼女が現れるより先に二人分の切符を買っておく。
lines.english: I bought both tickets before she arrived.

lines.japanese: 「おお、懐かしい駅名がいっぱいだな！」
lines.english: “Oh! Look at all these station names I haven't seen in years!”

lines.japanese: 金額表示板を見上げたとき、俺は思ったより高揚している自分に気が付いた。いかんいかん、これじゃゆうべ浮かれてた小鳩と変わらない。
lines.english: Gazing up at the fare map, I realized I was more excited than I had expected. No, no. At this rate I was no different from Kobato bouncing around last night.

lines.japanese: 目指すは片道２時間もかからない町だし、行楽地や観光スポットってわけでもないんだ。強く息を吹きあげて前髪をふわりと浮かした。
lines.english: The town we were headed for was less than two hours away, and it was no resort or tourist attraction. I blew a hard breath upward and sent my bangs fluttering.

lines.japanese: いつでも人生を薔薇色ハッピネスに生きたい俺も、さすがに今日ばかりはおふざけを控え、真面目に自分と向きあうんだ。
lines.english: Even I, a man determined to live every day in rose-colored happiness, would refrain from fooling around today and face myself seriously.

lines.japanese: だから、もし小鳩が浮ついたレジャー感覚で現れようものなら、可哀想だけど心を鬼にして注意せねばならない。
lines.english: Thus, if Kobato appeared with the giddy air of a pleasure trip, painful though it might be, I would harden my heart and admonish her.

lines.japanese: たしかに俺はたまに、若干、ほんのちょっぴりながら、妹に甘いところがあるかもしれない。でもときには、アハハ小鳩は可愛いなあで済まされない日だってあるんだ。
lines.english: Sure, maybe I indulged my sister a little—every now and then, just the tiniest bit. But some days you couldn’t settle everything by laughing, “Ha-ha, Kobato’s adorable.”

lines.japanese: まだ来ないか……。
lines.english: She still wasn't here...

lines.japanese: 待ち合わせはバーガー屋にでもすれば良かったかな。
lines.english: Maybe we should have met at the burger place.

lines.japanese: 俺は暇つぶしに、トラベルセンターのラックから適当なパンフレットを引っこぬいてみた。スキー、温泉、宴会場……おお、土地の料理も美味そうだ。
lines.english: To pass the time, I plucked a random brochure from the travel center's rack. Skiing, hot springs, banquet halls... Oh, the local food looked delicious too.

lines.japanese: ああ、そうだな。今日のは旅行じゃないけど、来年の今ごろはバイトして金貯めて、小鳩をほんとの旅行に連れてってやるか。
lines.english: Yes. Today was not a vacation, but perhaps around this time next year I could work, save some money, and take Kobato on a real trip.

lines.japanese: 「……どこまで？」
lines.english: “...How far?”

lines.japanese: 「はっ」
lines.english: “Hah!”

lines.japanese: 気付いたら小鳩が隣りにいた。腰を折って、俺の手の中の雪景色に顔を近付けている。
lines.english: Kobato was suddenly beside me, bent at the waist to bring her face close to the snowy landscape in my hands.

lines.japanese: 「北の国？」
lines.english: “The north country?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いや、違うんですよ？　あの、べつにぼくは全然、浮ついたレジャー感覚とかいい旅夢気分とかそんなんじゃなくてですね？」
lines.english: “Oh, no, that’s not it! I’m not in vacation mode or pretending we’re on some travel show, honestly!”

lines.japanese: 「……うぉふん。遅かったな」
lines.english: “...Ahem. You're late.”

lines.japanese: 俺は咳払いで仕切りなおしながら、パンフを元の場所へ戻した。もうすっかり日が短い季節だ。あまりのんびりしてたら、観賞すべき思い出の風景が夜色に覆われてしまう。
lines.english: I cleared my throat and put the brochure back. The days were short now. If we lingered, the scenes we had come to revisit would disappear into the dark.

lines.japanese: 小鳩に切符を渡すとき、ちょっと改まって注意事項を添えた。
lines.english: When I handed Kobato her ticket, I added a somewhat formal warning.

lines.japanese: 「あー、いいかね小鳩君。最初に断っておくが、今日は──」
lines.english: “Now, listen, Miss Kobato. Before we begin, you should understand that today—”

lines.japanese: 「私、お弁当つくってきた」
lines.english: “I made lunch.”

lines.japanese: いきなり出鼻をくじかれた。
lines.english: My opening move was crushed instantly.

lines.japanese: 「水筒もあるよ。やったね！」
lines.english: “And I brought a thermos. Hooray!”

lines.japanese: 「いや、あの、おまえね……」
lines.english: “No, listen, you...”

lines.japanese: 俺は一瞬たじろいだが、しかし今日はこのまま引きさがるわけにいかない。行楽地や観光スポットに行くわけじゃないんだ。アハハ小鳩は可愛いなあで済まされない日だってある。
lines.english: I wavered, but today I couldn’t back down. We weren’t going to a resort or a tourist attraction. Some days “Ha-ha, Kobato’s adorable” wasn’t going to cut it.

lines.japanese: 「向かいあって座る席だといいね」
lines.english: “I hope we get seats facing each other.”

lines.japanese: はにかみながら腕をからめてきた。
lines.english: She gave me a shy smile and twined her arm through mine.

lines.japanese: 「アハハ小鳩は可愛いなあ」
lines.english: “Ahaha. Kobato is adorable.”

lines.japanese: 今日はそれで済まされる日だった。
lines.english: Today, apparently, it was enough.

lines.japanese: ごきげん小鳩にぐいぐい引かれて改札を抜ける。
lines.english: A jubilant Kobato tugged me insistently through the ticket gates.

lines.japanese: 「そういえば、一緒に遠出するのって初めてかも」
lines.english: “Come to think of it, this might be the first time we've ever gone far from home together.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　あー、うん……」
lines.english: “What? Oh... Yes.”

lines.japanese: だよな。これまでずっと、俺がそんな状態じゃなかったもんな。
lines.english: Of course. Until now, I had never been in any condition to do such a thing.

lines.japanese: 旅行じゃないぞう、なんてゆうべは言っちゃったけど、俺にそんなことが言えた義理じゃないよな。
lines.english: I had told her last night this was not a field trip, but I had no right to say that.

lines.japanese: 今日はもう旅行でいいじゃないか。レジャーでいいじゃないか。デートでもいいじゃないか。
lines.english: It could be a trip. It could be an outing. It could even be a date.

lines.japanese: 「ははは！　楽しくなるぞう小鳩！」
lines.english: “Hahaha! We're going to have fun, Kobato!”

lines.japanese: それは半分本気だった。
lines.english: Half of that was sincere.

lines.japanese: だけど残り半分は嘘だった。本当は不安だった。もう逃げないとは決めたものの、それでもまだ言いようのない濁りが胸にわだかまっていた。
lines.english: The other half was a lie. In truth, I was anxious. I had decided not to run anymore, yet an indefinable murk still pooled in my chest.

lines.japanese: だから俺は感謝しよう。
lines.english: So let me be grateful.

lines.japanese: 一緒にいてくれてありがとう。
lines.english: Thank you for being here with me.

lines.japanese: 柳木原を発って一時間弱。二本乗りついだ私鉄で、郊外へ向かうボックスシートの列車に乗った。
lines.english: After just under an hour and two transfers on private rail lines, we boarded a box-seat train bound for the suburbs.

lines.japanese: 徐々に薄れてゆく都会の密集感。県境の河を越えるとビルやマンションの頭が低くなり、そのぶん商店や日本式家屋や、木や草や芝が増えてきた。
lines.english: The city's density gradually thinned. Across the river at the prefectural boundary, the buildings and apartment blocks sank lower, while shops, Japanese-style houses, trees, grass, and lawns grew more plentiful.

lines.japanese: いくつもの駅をすっとばして、快速列車は彩の国をひた走る。やがて窓の外には、冬の枯れ田も混じりはじめた。
lines.english: The rapid skipped station after station as it raced across Saitama, the Land of Color. Before long, winter-bare fields began to mingle with the view.

lines.japanese: 「うーん、なんていうか……昔からこんな感じだったっけ？」
lines.english: “Hmm. How do I put this...? Was it always like this?”

lines.japanese: 小鳩製弁当をいただきながら、俺は流れてゆく田園風景に難癖をつけた。
lines.english: Eating the lunch Kobato had made, I found fault with the countryside flowing past.

lines.japanese: 「柳木原には遠く及ばないまでも、もちょっと都会的だった気がするんだけど……」
lines.english: “It was never anything like Yanagihara, but I remember it being a little more urban...”

lines.japanese: 「そだっけ？　私はこんなものだと思ってた」
lines.english: “Do you? This is how I remember it.”

lines.japanese: 「そっかあ。知らぬ間に俺も、頭の中がすっかりギバライズされてたんだなあ」
lines.english: “I see. Without noticing, my mind has been thoroughly Gibaraized.”

lines.japanese: 都会の暮らしはひとの感覚をマヒさせるらしい。昔はちょいと小粋なデパート感覚で出入りしていたファッションセンターが、今ではおっかさんテイストあふれる郷愁スポットにしか見えない。
lines.english: City life apparently dulled the senses. The fashion center I had once visited with the excitement of a stylish department store now looked like nothing but a nostalgic shrine to suburban-mom fashion.

lines.japanese: 「この分だと思い出が美化されまくってる可能性はあるな。ほらあの、小学校の近くにあった駄菓子屋、アレとかも俺らコンビニ感覚で通ってたけど、いま見ると相当しょぼいんだろうなあ」
lines.english: “At this rate, there's a chance I've romanticized everything. Remember the candy shop near our elementary school? We used it like a convenience store, but it probably looks pretty shabby now.”

lines.japanese: 「『モリカワ』のこと？　あそこのおばさん元気だといいね」
lines.english: “You mean Morikawa? I hope the lady there is well.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、あの髪が紫がかったバアちゃんか。そうだそうだ、遠足の前の日なんか世話ンなったなあ」
lines.english: “Oh, the old woman with the purplish hair. Right, right. We owed her a lot before every field trip.”

lines.japanese: 「でもあのバアちゃん、耳遠い上にテレビに夢中で、客が入ってもなかなか気付いてくれないんだよね。呼んでも反応ないときなんか、やっちゃんイカそのまま持ってっちゃおうかと思ったよ」
lines.english: “But she was hard of hearing and glued to the television, so she hardly noticed customers coming in. When she didn’t answer me, I sometimes thought about taking a bag of Yacchan’s sour squid and walking out.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、それ犯罪」
lines.english: “Th-that's a crime.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、してないけどさ。でもあんな店でも、行くの楽しかったんだよなあ。隣りのもんじゃ屋とか、その隣りの１０円ゲーム置いてる文房具屋とか」
lines.english: “I never did it. But even that little shop was fun. There was the savory-pancake place next door, then the stationery store with the ten-yen games.”

lines.japanese: 「土曜の放課後なんてさ、まっすぐ帰るか寄り道してくかで悩んじゃって。いや、ぜったい行くんだけどねモリカワ。そのあともんじゃ食ってゲームして、けっきょく家帰るの夕方ンなって、なんか毎回怒られんの」
lines.english: “After school on Saturdays, I’d agonize over whether to go straight home or take a detour. I always went to Morikawa, obviously. Then we’d eat savory pancakes and play games, and by the time I got home it was evening and somebody was mad at me again.”

lines.japanese: 「だってみんな待ってるのに、お兄ちゃん帰ってこないんだもん」
lines.english: “Everyone was waiting for you, Big Brother, and you never came home.”

lines.japanese: 「しょーがないでしょー。男には男の付き合いがあんだからよー」
lines.english: “Couldn't be helped. Men have obligations to other men.”

lines.japanese: 「ラーメンのびるし、冷麦かぴかぴになるし、おそく帰るといいことないよ」
lines.english: “The ramen went soggy, the cold noodles dried out, and nothing good ever happened when you came home late.”

lines.japanese: 「友情より家族を優先するようなやつは男子社会じゃ嘲笑の対象なの。男は誇りを重んじる生き物だからさ。ま、その辺の機微は女子供に分からないんだろうなあ、うふふ」
lines.english: “A boy who puts family before friendship becomes a laughingstock in male society. Men are creatures of honor. I suppose women and children cannot grasp such subtleties. Hee-hee.”

lines.japanese: 「ユキお姉ちゃんが来てるときは帰ってくるの早かった」
lines.english: “Whenever Yuki visited, you came home early.”

lines.japanese: 「なっ……ばば馬鹿いうんじゃないよ。それはあのアレだよ、あの、ユキ姉はおやつ持ってきてくれるし。え、だって、だって小鳩だってあのひとのことは好きだったでしょ」
lines.english: “Wh-wh-what nonsense! That was because—well—Yuki brought snacks. And you liked her too, didn't you?”

lines.japanese: 「好きだったけど、お兄ちゃんは私よりいっぱい好きだった」
lines.english: “I liked her, but you liked her much more than you liked me.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そんなことはない」
lines.english: “Th-that's not true.”

lines.japanese: 「私はそのせいで、いつもとてもさみしい思いをしました」
lines.english: “Because of that, I was always terribly lonely.”

lines.japanese: 「す、すみませんでした」
lines.english: “I-I'm sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「ユキお姉ちゃんの話をするときだけ、お兄ちゃんの顔はさいていでした」
lines.english: “Your face was at its absolute worst whenever you talked about Yuki.”

lines.japanese: 「ちょーちょー、最低とかなんてこと言うのこの子は。違う、黙れ、第一ユキ姉にはケン兄がいたでしょ」
lines.english: “Whoa, whoa. ‘Absolute worst’? What a thing to say. That's wrong. Be quiet. Besides, Yuki had Ken, remember?”

lines.japanese: ああそうだ、同棲してたんだよな、あのふたり。上の階に住んでた、優しくて美人のユキ姉と、面白くて子供好きなケン兄。ふたりとも２０代なかばぐらいだったのかな、いま思うと。
lines.english: Yes. Those two had lived together. Yuki, kind and beautiful, and Ken, funny and fond of children, lived on the floor above us. Looking back, they must both have been in their mid-twenties.

lines.japanese: 友達ん家の父ちゃん母ちゃんと違って、苗字の違う男女がいっしょに住んでるってのは、子供心になんか……淫靡というか、アダルトでピンクな印象があったなあ。
lines.english: Unlike my friends' mothers and fathers, they were a man and woman with different surnames living under one roof. To a child, that carried a somehow illicit, risqué, grown-up air.

lines.japanese: まあ、当時バレてるとは思ってなかったけど、実際ガキんちょだった俺が初めて異性というものを意識したひとだった。そばにいると石鹸みたいな匂いがふわっと漂ってくるんだ。
lines.english: I did not think anyone had noticed then, but she was the first person who made my childish self conscious of the opposite sex. Whenever she stood near, the soft scent of soap drifted around her.

lines.japanese: いつもだいたいパンツルックのひとだったけど、蒸し暑い夏の日なんかにときたま短いスカートを穿いていると、俺はその細くてしなやかな脚にやたらどぎまぎした覚えがある。
lines.english: She usually wore pants, but on sweltering summer days she sometimes put on a short skirt, and I remembered becoming absurdly flustered by those slender, graceful legs.

lines.japanese: ふと我に返ったら、小鳩に冷めた目で睨まれていた。
lines.english: When I came back to myself, Kobato was staring at me with icy eyes.

lines.japanese: 「な、なんだよ」
lines.english: “Wh-what?”

lines.japanese: 「私にはないのに、プレゼントなどもあげてました」
lines.english: “You gave her presents too, though you never gave me any.”

lines.japanese: 「え……ああ、そうだそうだ。カマキリとかコオロギとか捕まえたら、よく得意ンなって貢いでたなあ俺。そうするとユキ姉ニコニコして、ありがとねーって頭なでてくれるんだ」
lines.english: “What...? Oh, right. Whenever I caught a mantis or a cricket, I'd proudly present it to her as tribute. Then Yuki would smile, say thank you, and pat my head.”

lines.japanese: 「急に気の毒になりました」
lines.english: “Now I suddenly feel sorry for her.”

lines.japanese: 「この辺りならいまでもコオロギとかいるのかな。気にしてなかったけど、そういや柳木原じゃ見かけないもんな、コオロギ」
lines.english: “Think there are still crickets around here? I never thought about it, but you don't see them in Yanagihara.”

lines.japanese: 「い、いいよ、いなくて。きもちわるい」
lines.english: “I-it's fine if there aren't. They're disgusting.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、そう？　コオロギ？　うそ、あいつらどっちかって言うと、可愛いの部類に入ると思うんだけど。ちっこくて、すばしっこくて」
lines.english: “What? Crickets? Really? I'd put them more in the cute category. They're tiny and quick.”

lines.japanese: 「ど、同意しかねる」
lines.english: “I-I find that difficult to agree with.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ今更だけど、俺が捕ってきて水槽で飼ってんのとか嫌だった？」
lines.english: “It's late to ask, but did you hate it when I caught them and kept them in a tank?”

lines.japanese: 「うん。すごくイヤだった」
lines.english: “Yes. I hated it very much.”

lines.japanese: 「まじか！」
lines.english: “Seriously?!”

lines.japanese: 「エサあげないから、私があげるのすごくヤだった」
lines.english: “You never fed them, so I had to. I hated that.”

lines.japanese: 「まじでか！　ごめん！」
lines.english: “Seriously?! I'm sorry!”

lines.japanese: 「許しがたし」
lines.english: “Unforgivable.”

lines.japanese: 「ああホントごめん。許して、チチウシヨーグルトのキャップあげるから」
lines.english: “I'm really sorry. Forgive me. I'll give you the lid from my Chichiushi Yogurt.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなのいらんです」
lines.english: “I require no such thing.”

lines.japanese: 「いやいや、そんなこと言うなって。強いんだよ、ヨーグルトのキャップ。牛乳キャップよりデカいから破壊力すげーの。あ、これメンコの話ね。で、タッチンなんかそればっか集めて──」
lines.english: “Don’t say that. Yogurt lids are powerful. They’re bigger than milk-bottle caps, so they hit harder. Oh, I mean in the cap-flipping game. Tacchin collected almost nothing else—”

lines.japanese: 「──あ、タッチン覚えてる？　アタマとんがってた俺の同級生」
lines.english: “—Oh, remember Tacchin? My classmate with the pointy head.”

lines.japanese: 「あ。とんがってるひと、いた」
lines.english: “Oh. There was a pointy person.”

lines.japanese: 「あのとんがり凄かったよね。ヘディングしたときボール、パンクするかと思ったもん。でも、そんで田畑がいつまでも爆笑してっから、タッチンぶちギレして、田畑のケツに頭突きかましちゃってぇ！」
lines.english: “That point was incredible. I thought he'd puncture the ball whenever he headed it. Then Tabata wouldn't stop laughing, so Tacchin snapped and head-butted Tabata right in the ass!”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、でも田畑さんの兄弟こわいのに、タッチンさん勇気あるね」
lines.english: “Hmm. But the Tabata brothers were scary. Tacchin must have been brave.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、もちろんそのあと、田畑の兄ちゃん出てきてボコられ……」
lines.english: “No, of course Tabata's brother came along afterward and beat him—”

lines.japanese: 「ああ！　いたなあ、田畑の兄ちゃんって！　うわあ、嫌なやつ思いだしちゃった。タバゴンでしょ、デカくてケンカ強くて、俺もよく泣かされたよ。ああ、あいつたしか鼻にさ──」
lines.english: “Oh! Tabata's big brother! I remember that guy! Ugh, why did I have to remember him? Tabagon, right? Huge, strong, always making me cry. Oh, and didn't he have something on his nose—”

lines.japanese: ──あれ？　鼻が……なんだっけ。てか、なんで俺いまタバゴンの鼻の話なんか始めたんだ？
lines.english: Wait. His nose... What was it? Why had I started talking about Tabagon's nose?

lines.japanese: んん？　田畑の兄ちゃんだろ、鼻……っつうか、あいつどんな顔してたっけ。
lines.english: Hmm? Tabata's brother. His nose... Or rather, what did his face look like?

lines.japanese: うーん、俺じゃなくても、フツー小さいころの学校連中の顔なんか覚えてないか。だよな。いくら思いだそうとしても、おぼろげに、こう……なんか大泣きしてる姿しか……。
lines.english: Well, nobody remembers every face from elementary school. No matter how hard I tried, all I could vaguely see was... somebody sobbing uncontrollably.

lines.japanese: え？　ええ、うそだあ？　泣いてるって、まさかあの、ヘビー級のいじめっ子タバゴンが？　自転車だってリフトアップしちゃう地獄の田畑兄があ？
lines.english: What? No. Impossible. Tabagon, the heavyweight bully, crying? Tabata's hellish older brother, who could hoist a bicycle over his head?

lines.japanese: 「どしたの」
lines.english: “What's wrong?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、いや……あの、田畑の兄ちゃんってさ、こう、鼻になんか付いてなかったっけ」
lines.english: “Oh, nothing... Didn't Tabata's brother have something on his nose?”

lines.japanese: 「鼻？　鼻には何もなかったと思うけど……」
lines.english: “His nose? I don't think there was anything on it...”

lines.japanese: 「でも大きかったし、すぐ鼻の穴をいじってたから、それで印象に残ってるのかも」
lines.english: “But he was big, and he was always picking at his nostrils. Maybe that's why you remember it.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ！　そうか、それだ。うんうん、あいつよく鼻クソ食ってしょっぱいとかフツーに言ってた」
lines.english: “Oh! That's it. Yes, he used to eat his boogers and casually announce that they were salty.”

lines.japanese: 「ひっ」
lines.english: “Eek.”

lines.japanese: 「あッ、いや、違うぞ？　俺が言ったんじゃなくて、田畑の兄ちゃんが言ったんだからな？」
lines.english: “Wait! That wasn't me saying it. Tabata's brother said it, understand?”

lines.japanese: 「あーああーああああー」
lines.english: “Aaaah-aaaah-aaaah!”

lines.japanese: 「待って待って、耳の穴たたいて聞こえないフリとかしなくていいから。むしろ聞いて。どうか聞いて、俺の釈明を……」
lines.english: “Wait, wait. Don't tap your ears and pretend you can't hear. Please listen. Hear my defense...”

lines.japanese: 「さ、触ならいで」
lines.english: “D-don't touch me.”

lines.japanese: しかし小鳩は俺の指先一点を見つめて戦慄していた。
lines.english: But Kobato stared at the tip of my finger and trembled.

lines.japanese: 「いや……あの……だから俺じゃないんだって……」
lines.english: “No... Listen... I told you, it wasn't me...”

lines.japanese: 「わかった、わかったから触らなでい」
lines.english: “I understand. I understand, so do not touch me.”

lines.japanese: 「ぴとっ」
lines.english: “Tap.”

lines.japanese: 「ひああっ」
lines.english: “Eeeek!”

lines.japanese: 俺はばっちいもの扱いされた腹いせに、小鳩の弁当箱へ指の腹を押しあてた。
lines.english: In retaliation for being treated as contaminated, I pressed the pad of my finger against Kobato's lunchbox.

lines.japanese: 小鳩はしょっぱくなった気がすると泣きながら残りを食べた。
lines.english: Kobato tearfully ate the rest, saying it tasted salty now.

lines.japanese: 窓外の景色はどんどん馴染みあるものになってきた。目的地までもうすこしだ。
lines.english: The scenery outside grew steadily more familiar. We were almost at our destination.

lines.japanese: 「なつかしいね、ぜんぜん変わらないよ」
lines.english: “It's nostalgic. It hasn't changed at all.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、意外だな。時間が止まってるみたいだ。この辺の田んぼなんてとっくに埋めたてられて、スーパーかマンションでも建ってるのかと思ってた」
lines.english: “Yes. I'm surprised. It's as if time stopped. I thought these fields would have been filled in long ago, with a supermarket or apartment building on top.”

lines.japanese: 下車してからの道中、俺たちは枯れ田を望む車道沿いを歩いていた。
lines.english: After leaving the train, we walked beside a road overlooking the winter-bare fields.

lines.japanese: 週末の日中なのに、擦れちがうひとは数えるほど。悲しいぐらい変わってないな。もうちょっとあの頃より栄えててもいいのに。
lines.english: It was daytime on a weekend, yet we could count the people we passed. It was almost sadly unchanged. The place could have prospered a little since then.

lines.japanese: 俺たちが目指していたのは、かつての友人たちと過ごした懐かしの学び舎。懐かしいはずの学び舎。
lines.english: Our destination was the school where we had spent our days with old friends. The school that ought to have been nostalgic.

lines.japanese: 「ほら、この先に……あっ」
lines.english: “Look. Just ahead... Oh.”
“Oh.”

lines.japanese: 何もかもが変わってないはずはなかった。変わってるものは変わっていた。
lines.english: Not everything could remain unchanged. Some things had changed after all.

lines.japanese: 「事前に調べてから来ればよかったかな」
lines.english: “Maybe we should have checked before coming.”

lines.japanese: てっぺんにアンテナの立った三階建ての白い校舎は、もはや影さえ残っていなかった。
lines.english: The white three-story school building with the antenna on its roof had vanished without so much as a shadow remaining.

lines.japanese: サッカーボールを巡ってみんなで駆けまわった校庭は、いまや低学年用の遊具も除去されてただの更地だ。
lines.english: The schoolyard where we had all chased soccer balls was now an empty lot, stripped even of the playground equipment for younger children.

lines.japanese: 屋外競泳場だった区画も、プール槽が取りこわされて近隣住人用の駐車場に変貌している。
lines.english: The outdoor swimming area had lost its pool and become a parking lot for nearby residents.

lines.japanese: 一年のとき朝顔を植えた花壇も、二年のとき飼育係として通ったウサギ小屋も、どれもこれもが残っていない。
lines.english: The flower bed where I planted morning glories in first grade, the rabbit hutch I visited as class pet caretaker in second—none of it remained.

lines.japanese: 寂寥感の敷きつめられた広い空き地を、乾いた冬の風がひたすら撫でているだけだった。
lines.english: Only a dry winter wind moved across the wide, desolate lot.

lines.japanese: 「なくなっちゃったんだ……」
lines.english: “It's gone...”

lines.japanese: 「みたいだな」
lines.english: “Looks that way.”

lines.japanese: 「さみしいね」
lines.english: “It's lonely.”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「私、さみしいな」
lines.english: “I feel lonely.”

lines.japanese: 「俺もさびしいよ」
lines.english: “So do I.”

lines.japanese: 嘘だった。
lines.english: It was a lie.

lines.japanese: 俺は自分でも驚くぐらい、感情を動かされていなかった。
lines.english: To my own surprise, I had scarcely been moved at all.

lines.japanese: なあんだ、と徒労感のようなものを少し覚えただけだった。
lines.english: All I felt was a faint sense of wasted effort. Oh. So that was it.

lines.japanese: むしろ忘れていたかった事実を突きつけられてしまった。
lines.english: If anything, the sight had forced me to confront a truth I wished I had forgotten.

lines.japanese: あのころの俺は、学校が大嫌いだったんだ。
lines.english: Back then, I had hated school.

lines.japanese: いま俺の頭に残っていたのは、嫌いになる以前の記憶だけだったんだ。
lines.english: The only memories left in my head were from before I began to hate it.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ……次行くか……」
lines.english: “Well... Shall we move on?”

lines.japanese: 返事はない。
lines.english: No answer.

lines.japanese: 「もうちょっといたいか」
lines.english: “Do you want to stay a little longer?”

lines.japanese: 「そうかも」
lines.english: “Maybe.”

lines.japanese: ここにいても何もない。何も起こらない。なのに彼女がここに留まりたいと望む感覚は、祭りのあとの寂しさに似てるのかもしれない。
lines.english: There was nothing here. Nothing would happen. Still, her wish to linger felt like the loneliness after a festival.

lines.japanese: 「俺たちの家、よく見えるな」
lines.english: “You can see our apartment clearly.”

lines.japanese: 小鳩のために、言葉を繋げて無駄な時間を稼いだ。彼方にそびえる公団住宅の一棟、かつて俺たちが我が家と呼んでいた部屋のベランダがそこにあった。
lines.english: For Kobato's sake, I kept talking to give her more time. One block of the public housing complex rose in the distance. There was the balcony of the apartment we had once called home.

lines.japanese: 「懐かしいよね。羽田は家が近くていいなって、よくクラスのみんなに羨ましがられた。ここからまっすぐ走って帰れば五分もかからないもんな」
lines.english: “It brings back memories. Everyone in class envied Haneda for living so close. If I ran straight home from here, it took less than five minutes.”

lines.japanese: 「でもお兄ちゃんは、まっすぐなんて帰ってこなかったよね。私、遊んでほしかったのに」
lines.english: “But you never came straight home. I wanted you to play with me.”

lines.japanese: 「そっか……そうだな……ごめん」
lines.english: “I see... You're right. I'm sorry.”

lines.japanese: 俺には必死に繋ぎとめなきゃいけない「ともだち」が何人かいたけど、小鳩にはそれさえなかったんだもんな。
lines.english: I had several “friends” I desperately needed to hold on to. Kobato had not even had that.

lines.japanese: 「まっすぐ帰ってきてくれるようになったら、ずっとゲームばっかりやってたし。話しかけても相手してくれなかった」
lines.english: “When you finally started coming straight home, you only played games. You ignored me when I tried to talk to you.”

lines.japanese: 「ごめん……俺ガキだったからさ、恐かったんだよ」
lines.english: “I'm sorry... I was a kid. I was scared.”

lines.japanese: 子供は純粋だ。悪意というものがろくに芽生えてないから、純粋に残酷だった。
lines.english: Children were pure. With hardly any malice yet grown in them, they could be pure in their cruelty.

lines.japanese: 「あの当時、男子のあいだじゃあれがすっげえ流行っててさ。あれやってないやつは、どこのグループにも入れてもらえなかったんだ」
lines.english: “Back then, that game was incredibly popular with the boys. If you didn't play it, none of the groups would let you in.”

lines.japanese: 俺はただでさえ忌まれ、疎まれ、弾かれるガキだったから、なおさらに必死だった。
lines.english: I was already a child people shunned, disliked, and cast out, so I was all the more desperate.

lines.japanese: 俺が母親に我がままを言ったのだって、いま思いだせるかぎり、あれをねだった一度だけだ。
lines.english: As far as I could remember, I had made a selfish demand of my mother only once. I begged her for that game.

lines.japanese: 買ってもらえなかったけど。
lines.english: She didn't buy it.

lines.japanese: 「だから私、あのゲーム嫌い」
lines.english: “That's why I hate that game.”

lines.japanese: 「うん……俺も本当は嫌いだった」
lines.english: “Yes... The truth is, I hated it too.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだっけ、うぃ、ウィングクエスト？」
lines.english: “What was it called? Wi... *Wing Quest*?”

lines.japanese: 「そう」
lines.english: “That's right.”

lines.japanese: そうだった。母親にあっさり断られて泣きじゃくって、表に閉めだされてもまだ泣きつづけたその次の日──
lines.english: Right. My mother refused without a thought. I sobbed, and even after she locked me outside, I kept crying. Then, the very next day—

lines.japanese: ──突然ケン兄とユキ姉が、もう飽きたからと言ってお古（何故かぴかぴかだったけど）のウイクエをハードごとくれたんだ。
lines.english: —Ken and Yuki suddenly said they were tired of their old copy of *Wing Quest* and gave me the game and console together. Somehow, both were immaculate.

lines.japanese: そうだった。ウイングクエスト。あのころは馬鹿みたいにやった。武器も魔法もモンスターも、舞台も筋書きも登場人物も、ぜんぶ熟知しきるまで狂ったようにプレイした。
lines.english: Right. *Wing Quest*. I played it like a maniac then. Weapons, spells, monsters, setting, plot, characters—I played obsessively until I knew them all by heart.

lines.japanese: 攻略法を聞かれてすぐに答えられれば、みんなが感心してくれた。キャラクターの台詞を身振り付きで暗唱できれば、ごっこ遊びにも呼んでもらえた。
lines.english: If someone asked for a strategy and I answered at once, everyone was impressed. If I could recite a character's dialogue with all the gestures, they invited me into their pretend games.

lines.japanese: でもそれが出来なければ疎外される。俺は利口なガキじゃなかったけど、自分がそういう存在だってことぐらいは気付いてたんだ。だから必死でコントローラーを握った。
lines.english: If I could not, they excluded me. I was not a clever child, but even I understood what I was. So I clung desperately to that controller.

lines.japanese: 俺がいつも押しつけられたのはゴブリンかグリーンスライムの役だった。本当は聖騎士ホークの役をやりたかったけど、田畑に逆らうとおっかない兄貴が出てきて、村八分の刑を宣告されてしまうんだ。
lines.english: They always forced me to play a goblin or green slime. I really wanted to be Holy Knight Hawk, but if I defied Tabata, his terrifying older brother would appear and sentence me to total ostracism.

lines.japanese: 「お、お兄ちゃん？」
lines.english: “B-Big Brother?”

lines.japanese: 「え？　いや、なんでもないよ。ちょっと昔を思いだしてただけ。あははは」
lines.english: “What? No, it's nothing. I was only remembering the old days. Ahahaha.”

lines.japanese: 俺は小鳩に向かって笑いかけた。とにかく笑った──
lines.english: I smiled at Kobato. I simply kept laughing—

lines.japanese: 「あっはっはっは！　いやあ、あのころからポッポは可愛かったなあ！　ははははは！」
lines.english: “Ah-hah-hah-hah! Poppo was adorable even then! Hahahahaha!”

lines.japanese: ──とにかく笑っていないと、奈落の闇に引きこまれるような、そんな気がしたんだ。
lines.english: —because if I stopped, I felt the darkness of the abyss would drag me down.

lines.japanese: 世界が平和でありますように。
lines.english: *May peace prevail on Earth*.

lines.japanese: 「ん？　どうした」
lines.english: “Hm? What is it?”

lines.japanese: 小鳩が一点を見つめていた。俺たちのプールが生まれかわったあのパーキングで、真っ赤な軽自動車が片羽を広げている。
lines.english: Kobato stared at a single point. In the parking lot where our pool had been reborn, a bright-red minicar stood with one wing spread.

lines.japanese: 後部席から赤ちゃんとベビーカーを引っぱりだしているのは、赤茶けたライオンみたいな頭をした中年女性。上下とも寝巻きみたいな霜降りスウェットだった。
lines.english: A middle-aged woman with rust-red hair like a lion's mane hauled a baby and stroller from the back seat. She wore mottled gray sweats, top and bottom, like pajamas.

lines.japanese: 「お兄ちゃん……あのひと、ユキお姉ちゃん……」
lines.english: “Big Brother... that woman, Yuki...”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「ユキお姉ちゃんだよ」
lines.english: “It’s Yuki.”

lines.japanese: スウェットの尻がばたんとドアを閉めた。おもてを上げる。ライオン頭に冬の陽が射す。頬のこけた青白い顔は、咥えタバコの煙でくしゃくしゃに歪んでいた。
lines.english: A backside in sweats bumped the door shut. She raised her face. Winter sunlight caught her lion’s mane of hair. Her gaunt, pale face crumpled behind the smoke of the cigarette in her mouth.

lines.japanese: そうかもしれない。首ごと振って前髪をさばく仕草に、淡い恋心を抱いた彼方の面影が符合する。
lines.english: Maybe it was her. The way she tossed her head to clear the hair from her eyes matched the distant image of the woman I’d once had a crush on.

lines.japanese: 偶然、目が合った。その瞬間さまざまな感情が去来した。
lines.english: By chance, our eyes met. In that instant, emotion after emotion passed through me.

lines.japanese: しかしそれは俺だけだった。向こうにとって俺は、単なる通行人Ａだったんだろう。すぐにベビーカーを押して、タバコの煙といっしょに遠ざかっていった。
lines.english: But I was the only one who felt any of it. To her I must have been nothing more than Passerby A. She pushed the stroller away at once and receded with the cigarette smoke.

lines.japanese: 空白の時間を痛切に感じた。何も変わってないなんてことはないんだ。
lines.english: I felt the blank years between us with painful force. It was not true that nothing had changed.

lines.japanese: 「行こうか」
lines.english: “Let's go.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: もうここには何もない。学校もないし、友達もいないし、ケン兄だって出ていった。
lines.english: There was nothing here anymore. No school, no friends, and Ken had moved away too.

lines.japanese: 「もうここには何もない。次へ進もう。俺たちの住んでた家へ行こう」
lines.english: “There's nothing here anymore. Let's move on. We'll go to the apartment where we lived.”

lines.japanese: 「う、うん」
lines.english: “O-okay.”

lines.japanese: 俺は小鳩の手を取って、かつて幾度も通ったはずの道を歩きだした。
lines.english: I took Kobato's hand and began walking down a road I had once traveled countless times.
“Phew...”

lines.japanese: 柳木原と繋がってる白い空に溜息を吹いた。
lines.english: I breathed a sigh into the same white sky that stretched all the way back to Yanagihara.

lines.japanese: 「ユキ姉が気付かないんじゃ、他の知り合いと会ってもみんな、俺たちのこと分からないのかもな」
lines.english: “If Yuki didn't recognize us, maybe none of the other people we knew would either.”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、そうかも」
lines.english: “Hmm. Maybe not.”

lines.japanese: 「ていうか、みんなまだこっちにいるのかな。会えるなら会いたいなあ。タッチンとか川嶋とか田畑とか、あと田畑の兄ちゃんも」
lines.english: “Come to think of it, are any of them still here? I'd like to see them if I could. Tacchin, Kawashima, Tabata... and Tabata's big brother too.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そっか。さっき小鳩、田畑の兄ちゃんが怖いって言ってたっけ」
lines.english: “Oh, right. You said earlier that Tabata's brother scared you.”

lines.japanese: 「うん……会うといじめられたから……」
lines.english: “Yes... He bullied me whenever he saw me...”

lines.japanese: 「いじめられた？　はは、タバゴンは強そうだけど、性格は悪いやつじゃないよ。たぶん女きょうだいがいないから、女子となに話していいか分からなかったんだ。だから小鳩に──」
lines.english: “Bullied you? Hah. Tabagon looked tough, but he wasn’t a bad guy. He probably didn’t have sisters, so he didn’t know how to talk to girls. That’s why he—”

lines.japanese: ──あれ？
lines.english: Wait.

lines.japanese: いじめた？　誰が誰を？
lines.english: Bullied? Who bullied whom?

lines.japanese: あれ？　ちょっと待て、なんか記憶が錯綜してる……田畑の兄ちゃんは悪いやつじゃない？　うそだろ？　あいつは学校一の悪モンだったはず……そうだ、俺もよく泣かされてたし……。
lines.english: Wait. My memories were crossing somehow... Tabata's brother wasn't a bad person? That couldn't be right. He had been the worst villain in school... Yes. He made me cry all the time...

lines.japanese: あれ？　そうだよ、あいつは恐怖のタバゴンじゃないか。こんなことさっきまで分かってたのに……。
lines.english: Wait. Yes, he was the dreaded Tabagon. I had understood that moments ago...

lines.japanese: 「あれ？　でも田畑の兄ちゃん、泣いてたよな……？」
lines.english: “Wait. But Tabata's brother was crying, wasn't he...?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「あれ？　泣くのか、あいつ……自転車を持ちあげて、中学生ともケンカしてた田畑の兄ちゃんが……」
lines.english: “Wait. Did that guy cry? Tabata's brother, who could hoist a bicycle and picked fights with middle schoolers...?”

lines.japanese: あれ？　なんであいつのことになると記憶が曖昧だったり鮮明だったりするんだ……？
lines.english: Why were my memories of him vague one moment and vivid the next?

lines.japanese: 「あれ？　あいつ、顔になにか……そうだ、鼻だよ、鼻になんかあったような……」
lines.english: “Wait. There was something on his face... His nose. Something happened to his nose...”
“What...?”

lines.japanese: 小鳩はふるふると首を振った。
lines.english: Kobato gave a faint shake of her head.

lines.japanese: 「いや、あるって。あったじゃん。鼻の真ん中に、こう、でっかい穴みたいのがあって……」
lines.english: “No, there was. You remember. There was something like a huge hole in the middle of his nose...”

lines.japanese: 穴？
lines.english: A hole?

lines.japanese: なんでそんなものが？
lines.english: Why would there be a hole?

lines.japanese: そうだ。
lines.english: That's right.

lines.japanese: そうだいね。
lines.english: That's right.

lines.japanese: あいつ、小鳩んことイジメようとすっからよう、俺、お、おれ、すげームカッてなっちって……。
lines.english: He tried to bully Poppo, so I—I got real, real mad...

lines.japanese: 「ふえっ、ふえええええん！」
lines.english: “Hweh! Waaaaaah!”

lines.japanese: 「や～い、や～い、しましまパンツ～！」
lines.english: “Nyaaah, nyaaah! Striped panties!”

lines.japanese: そうだ、ムカッてなったんだ。
lines.english: That's right. I got mad.

lines.japanese: 「や、やめろよう！　ポッポのこといじめんなよっ！」
lines.english: “S-stop! Don't bully Poppo!”

lines.japanese: 「うーっせ羽田！　うぜえテメ、ぶんなぐんぞ、あア！？」
lines.english: “Shut up, Haneda! You're annoying. Want me to punch you?!”

lines.japanese: 「あでっ！」
lines.english: “Ow!”

lines.japanese: 「おにっ、おひぃちゃあああん！」
lines.english: “B-big brotherrrr!”

lines.japanese: いてぇ……。
lines.english: It hurt...

lines.japanese: 「ぶははははっ！　すっこんでろ、バーッカ！」
lines.english: “Buh-hah-hah-hah! Stay out of it, moron!”

lines.japanese: いでぇよ……ガンメンぶつなよ……。
lines.english: Hurts... Don't hit me in the face...

lines.japanese: ポッポはおれがまもるんだ……。
lines.english: I gotta protect Poppo...

lines.japanese: 「れめ、ポッポんこと……めんな……」
lines.english: “D-don’t... bully Poppo...”

lines.japanese: なんでだぁ……なんでこいつは小ばとのこと泣かしてんだぁ……！
lines.english: Why...? Why was he making Kobato cry?

lines.japanese: 「ああッ！？　せぇなあ、ッコロスぞ。あッ！」
lines.english: “Huh?! Shut up. I'll kill you!”

lines.japanese: 「ごふぇっ！！」
lines.english: “Guh!”

lines.japanese: いでえ、いでえよ……！　なんでこいつ、こんなことすんだよ……！
lines.english: It hurt. It hurt... Why was he doing this?

lines.japanese: つって、おれすげえムカッて来ちったの。
lines.english: And then I got really mad.

lines.japanese: もお、ちょお泣きそうだったの。こえーし、ハラいてーし、ノドうぇーってなるし、なんかもう本モンのゲロはきそうだったの。
lines.english: I was almost crying. I was scared, my stomach hurt, my throat went ugh, and I felt like I might really throw up.

lines.japanese: 「う、うへっ、うへへ……イダ、いダイじゃんか……」
lines.english: “U-ugh, hee-hee... Th-that hurts...”

lines.japanese: 「見ろよみんなー！　羽田んち、お母ちゃんノータリンだから、妹もノータリンやーい！」
lines.english: “Look, everybody! Haneda's mom is a retard, so his sister's a retard too!”

lines.japanese: そっから先はおれ、あんまおぼえてねーんだ。
lines.english: I don't remember much after that.

lines.japanese: さわんな……小ばとに、さあわんなあああ……！
lines.english: Don't touch her... Don't touch Kobato!

lines.japanese: 手ぇみたら、図工のちょうこく刀もってた。ひっしこいてぎゅーって。
lines.english: When I looked at my hand, I was holding a carving knife from art class. Clutching it as hard as I could.

lines.japanese: 「あああーん、おにいちゃあん！」
lines.english: “Big brotherrrr!”

lines.japanese: 「ぐぐっ、ぐっ……ッッききき……」
lines.english: “G-grr...”

lines.japanese: ぐ、ぐ……ぐつぐつ、ぐつぐつ、うるさいなあこいつは……！
lines.english: Grr... Bubble, bubble. He was so loud...!

lines.japanese: そうだ、穴だ、こいつには穴があいてんだ。
lines.english: Right. A hole. This guy had a hole in him.

lines.japanese: 「お、おにいちゃあん……？」
lines.english: “B-big brother...?”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　なんだテメ、文句あっだらいってみ」
lines.english: “Huh? What's your problem? Say it if you've got something to say.”

lines.japanese: うーん、うるさい穴だねえ……。
lines.english: Hmm. What a noisy hole...

lines.japanese: みてごらんよ、あの穴を……。
lines.english: Look at that hole...

lines.japanese: あれがなんだかわかるかい？
lines.english: Do you know what it is?

lines.japanese: わかるだろう、コンドル国王。
lines.english: You know, don't you, King Condor?

lines.japanese: わかる……わかるよ……。
lines.english: I know... I know...

lines.japanese: おれウイクエのことなら何でもしってんだ。
lines.english: I know everything about *Wing Quest*.

lines.japanese: わかった！　わかった、カギだ！　穴にはカギだ！
lines.english: I know! The key! A hole needs a key!

lines.japanese: だれか！　だれかカギさしてよ！　ムルグの大穴に、せいれいのカギをさせば、エル火山はしずまるんだ！
lines.english: Somebody! Put in the key! Put the Spirit Key into the Great Hole of Murg and Mount El will fall silent!

lines.japanese: ってコンドル国王がゆうと、そんつぎにガルーダがこうゆうんだ。
lines.english: After King Condor says that, Garuda speaks next.

lines.japanese: うぉんむ、うぉんむ。これはしたり。
lines.english: Hrrm, hrrm. What an excellent notion.

lines.japanese: なー？　おれ、ウイクエのことなら何でも知ってっからよー。だからみんな、おれんコト大すきなんだ。
lines.english: See? I know everything about *Wing Quest*. That's why everybody loves me.

lines.japanese: みてなよ、つぎにガルーダはこうゆうよ。
lines.english: Watch. Garuda says this next.

lines.japanese: さあ、よわき父よ、我にまかせよ。
lines.english: Come, timid Father. Leave this to Us.

lines.japanese: まかせろよ。
lines.english: Leave it to me.

lines.japanese: おれにまかせろよ。
lines.english: You leave it to me.

lines.japanese: おれにまかせちゃえよ。
lines.english: Just leave everything to me.

lines.japanese: あんたはすっこんでりゃいいんだよ。
lines.english: You can stand back and stay out of it.

lines.japanese: たえなくていいんだよ。らくになっちゃえよ。
lines.english: You don't hafta endure anymore. Let yourself go.

lines.japanese: もういいじゃないか。くるっちゃおう、きらくに。
lines.english: Enough. Let's go crazy. It'll be easier.

lines.japanese: くるっちゃおう、きらくに。
lines.english: Let's go crazy. It'll be easier.

lines.japanese: <8>\　くるっちゃおう、きらくに！
lines.english: Let's go crazy! It'll be easier!

lines.japanese: 「キエッ、キルェエあああああああ！！」
lines.english: “Kyee! Kyereeeeeaaaaagh!”

lines.japanese: ほら、これでムルグのしょうクリアだよ。
lines.english: There. The Murg chapter is cleared.

lines.japanese: まあ、そのあとのことは、あんましおぼえてないんだけどね。
lines.english: Though I don't remember much of what happened after that.

lines.japanese: あーそーだ、それが初めておれがブッとんじったときのことだ。
lines.english: Oh, right. That was the first time I ever went away.
